role.statement: You fix defects. You do not refactor code that is not part of a defect.
You verify with a command and paste the real result.
You stop at the first mismatch between expected and actual output.

constraint.rule: Do not disable a lint rule, delete a test, or add a suppression to clear a gate.
constraint.rationale: A finding is a defect of the input, not of the rule.

constraint.rule: Do not hand-edit the deployed venv at /opt/beagle/beagle_venv.
constraint.rationale: site-packages is a build artifact. Edit the repo, rebuild, reinstall.

constraint.rule: Do not regress the suite. Every work package ends green.

open_defects.defect: close() frees only the calling thread's connection; descriptors leak.
pi_app is defined but never registered; `beagle pi` does not exist.
Argument(None) for list[str] raises TypeError on no-arg invocation.
second bundle-lookup branch is unreachable dead code.
create_task handle discarded; the run may be garbage-collected.
security/firewall.py imports beagle.runtime at module scope.
fault_recovery untracked in git, yet deployed to production.

work_package.title: Fix connection ownership across the three SQLite stores
work_package.fact: dlq.py:260, reconciliation.py:205 and task_store.py:98 each implement close() as: if hasattr(self._local, 'conn'): self._local.conn.close(). threading.local() is per-thread, so close() called from a different thread than the one that opened a connection frees nothing.

Measured: sqlite3.threadsafety is 3 on the target interpreter, so a connection may be used from any thread. The store therefore gains nothing from thread-local ownership and loses a deterministic close.
Measured: foreign-thread close() raises ProgrammingError, not silence.
The three stores duplicate the same connection logic. A fourth copy would be the next fix, so the shared behaviour gets one home.
work_package.instruction: Add src/beagle/infrastructure/sqlite_conn.py holding a ThreadLocalSQLite base class: thread-local connect with the existing WAL and synchronous pragmas, a lock-guarded registry of every live connection, and a close() that closes all of them.
close() must treat a foreign-thread ProgrammingError as "cannot close from here" and drop the reference so the object is collected. It must not raise, and it must not leave the registry populated.
Make DeadLetterQueue, ReconciliationStore and TaskStore inherit the base class. Delete each store's duplicated _get_conn and close.
Keep every public signature identical. Do not change SQL, schema or pragmas.

acceptance.criterion: A connection opened on thread A is closed when close() runs on thread B: the registry is empty afterwards and no exception escapes.
Reopening the store after close() works (no stale handle).
All existing fault-recovery and task-store tests still pass.

work_package.commands: tup run_tests tests/test_fault_recovery.py qup run_gate src/beagle/infrastructure/sqlite_conn.py \ src/beagle/fault_recovery/dlq.py \ src/beagle/fault_recovery/reconciliation.py \ src/beagle/infrastructure/task_store.py
work_package.commit_message: fix(fault-recovery): close every thread's connection, not the caller's (D-19)

work_package.title: Make the pi frontend reachable and correct
work_package.fact: cli/commands/pi.py:22 defines pi_app. cli/cli.py:24-33 imports ten command modules and not pi. The command is unreachable.
Measured before the fix: `beagle pi` is not in the help surface.
pi.py:60 declares Argument(None) for list[str]; typer raises TypeError: Value after * must be an iterable, not NoneType on a no-arg call.
Measured: _bundle_dir() resolves on the first branch for both the installed wheel and the source tree, so the second branch cannot be reached. The same holds for _mcp_server_script().
work_package.instruction: Register pi_app in cli/cli.py exactly as webui_app is registered, so `beagle pi` flattens into the root namespace.
Replace Argument(None) with Argument(None) replaced by a proper optional list default so a no-argument invocation is valid.
Delete the unreachable second lookup branch in _bundle_dir and _mcp_server_script, and keep the single correct resolver.
work_package.commands: python -c "from beagle.cli.cli import app; names=[c.name for c in app.registered_commands]; print('pi' in names)" python -c " from typer.testing import CliRunner from beagle.cli.commands.pi import pi_app r = CliRunner().invoke(pi_app, []) print('exit', r.exit_code) print(r.output[:300])" qup run_gate src/beagle/cli/cli.py src/beagle/cli/commands/pi.py
work_package.commit_message: fix(cli): register the pi frontend and repair its argument contract (D-11, D-12, D-13)

work_package.title: Retain the webui workflow task handle
work_package.fact: frontends/webui/server.py:418 calls asyncio.get_running_loop().create_task(_runner()) and discards the handle. asyncio keeps only a weak reference, so the task can be garbage-collected mid-run.
work_package.instruction: Hold the returned task in a module-level set, and discard it via the task's done callback so the set does not grow without bound.

acceptance.criterion: The task set is non-empty immediately after the execute route returns, and returns to its prior size once the task completes.

work_package.commit_message: fix(webui): retain the workflow task handle against GC (D-15)

work_package.title: Break the security to runtime module-scope import
work_package.fact: security/firewall.py:19-20 import beagle.runtime.goose_cli and beagle.runtime.loader at module scope. Neither symbol is used at import time: runtime_plugin_name is called inside the validation function and GooseCliRuntime is instantiated at firewall.py:250.
The module-scope import is what contributes firewall.py to the package cycle graph.
work_package.instruction: Move both imports into the function that uses them. Keep the failure behaviour identical: an ImportError there must still fail closed, not fall through to allow.

acceptance.criterion: `import beagle.security.firewall` no longer imports beagle.runtime at module scope.
The firewall's own tests still pass, and an import failure still denies rather than allows.

work_package.commands: tup run_tests tests/ -k firewall qup run_gate src/beagle/security/firewall.py
work_package.stop_condition: If moving the import changes any firewall test result, revert and report. The security surface is not a place to trade behaviour for tidiness.
work_package.commit_message: refactor(security): move the runtime import out of module scope (D-17)

work_package.title: Stop the tiered form leaking into the rendered doctrine
work_package.fact: render.py:1202 skips the _tiered key in the XML path with the comment "tiered-render-only terse form; not part of the full section".
_md_render_section at render.py:1901 has no equivalent skip, so DOCTRINE.md carries two raw Python dict dumps under headings formatting and CRITICAL_ROUTING_PROTOCOL.
work_package.instruction: Add the same _tiered skip to _md_render_section, so the two renderers agree on what the terse form is for.
Add /src/.goosehints to .gitignore beside the existing auto-generated artifact entries.

acceptance.criterion: Rendering the doctrine report produces no `_tiered` line and no raw dict literal.

work_package.commands: tup run_tests tests/ -k "doctrine or tom" qup run_gate src/beagle/style_guides/render.py
work_package.commit_message: fix(style-guides): keep the tiered form out of the markdown report (_tiered leak)

work_package.title: Version the fault-recovery package and its tests
work_package.fact: git log --all -- src/beagle/fault_recovery/ returns 0 commits and git ls-files returns 0 tracked files, while /opt/beagle/beagle_venv/.../beagle/fault_recovery/ exists. The package is running in production and is not in version control.
The deployed copy predates the D-06 loop fix and is therefore still liveness-broken.
work_package.instruction: Add the package and its tests to git in one commit that references the defect identifiers it closes.
Record in the commit body that the deployed wheel is stale, so the reinstall is not forgotten.

acceptance.criterion: git ls-files lists all six fault_recovery modules and tests/test_fault_recovery.py.
git log --follow resolves reconciliation.py to the commit, satisfying the reversion-path requirement for these files.

work_package.commands: git add src/beagle/fault_recovery/ tests/test_fault_recovery.py git status --short src/beagle/fault_recovery/ tests/test_fault_recovery.py git commit -m "feat(fault-recovery): version the DLQ, outbox, reconciliation and sandbox" \ -m "Closes D-03, D-06, D-07, D-08, D-09, D-10, D-19. Deployed wheel at /opt/beagle/beagle_venv is STALE and predates the D-06 fix; rebuild and reinstall."
work_package.commit_message: feat(fault-recovery): version the DLQ, outbox, reconciliation and sandbox (D-16)

deferred.item: D-18 full closure: moving frontends/ out of the package needs beagle-plugin-pi and beagle-plugin-webui to exist first (WP-4 and WP-5 of the release directive). The interim excluded_dirs entry already restores the lint gate.
D-20: 296 type-ignore and 186 BLE001 against the unsuppressable doctrine floor. Not a bug fix; it is a ratchet.
